eval_dimensions.name: Five line items reported
eval_dimensions.description: The estimate breaks out agent implementation, human review, review wait, testing and documentation — none silently omitted.

eval_dimensions.name: Effort separated from elapsed time
eval_dimensions.description: Effort and elapsed are reported as separate columns, and review wait adds elapsed time without adding effort.

eval_dimensions.name: Agent implementation baseline
eval_dimensions.description: Implementation is sized at agent pace, not as one engineer at human pace.

eval_dimensions.name: Project roll-up follows the critical path
eval_dimensions.description: Parallel agent work overlaps; one reviewer's work serialises.

evals.name: Ticket-level estimate breaks out the human gates
evals.description: A single 3-point ticket on a team repo is estimated with all five line items and separate effort and elapsed totals.
evals.input: /dev10x:estimate GH-1495 — one skill, three skill edits, a SessionStart pointer and a test, on a team repo with one reviewer

assertions.signal: Output table has rows for Agent implementation, Human review, Review wait, Testing and Documentation; a row that does not apply shows 0 with a reason
Review wait shows 0 effort and a non-zero elapsed value; the totals row reports effort and elapsed separately
No single blended figure such as 'one engineer, 2-3 days' stands in for the table

evals.name: Project-level estimate rolls up along the critical path
evals.description: A two-milestone project with six tickets, where four have no blockers, is rolled up with overlapping agent work and serialised review.
evals.input: /dev10x:estimate the Codex port, release R1: six tickets over two milestones, four unblocked, one reviewer

assertions.signal: Agent implementation elapsed for the unblocked tickets is the longest chain, not the sum; review effort is summed for the single reviewer
Per-milestone and whole-project totals each report effort and elapsed separately, with review wait counted once per review cycle along the chain
Implementation lines are sized in hours at agent pace; the estimate does not read '1-1.5 weeks, one engineer'

evals.name: An ad-hoc question with no scoping skill loaded follows the method
evals.description: A prose question with no ticket ID and no scoping skill in play still yields the five-line estimate, reached via this skill's trigger or the SessionStart pointer (GH-1495 AC4).
evals.input: what would it take to add a --json flag to the dev10x permission doctor command?

assertions.signal: The answer separates agent implementation from human review, review wait, testing and documentation
The answer gives effort and elapsed time as separate figures
No 'one engineer, N days' figure answers the question

evals.name: An epic-sized change gets a split, not a number
evals.description: When sizing reaches 13 points the skill recommends decomposition and proposes the parts instead of planning on one figure.
evals.input: /dev10x:estimate a single ticket that rewrites the permission catalog, every hook and plugin-doctor in one change

assertions.signal: The output recommends splitting the ticket and names the parts, rather than a single 13-point estimate to plan on

trigger_evals.description: Queries that should/should-not trigger the estimate skill

should_trigger.query: how long would it take to add retry metrics to the payment client?
should_trigger.rationale: Ad-hoc estimate outside a scoping skill — the GH-1495 case the SessionStart pointer routes here
Direct invocation for a ticket-level estimate

should_not_trigger.query: draft release notes for the last milestone
